title: CostWeave – probabilistic workload profiler & continuous batch parameter weaver
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description:
Goal: Build CostWeave, a recommender that continuously profiles production workloads (per-customer and per-route) and synthesizes probabilistic batching and KV-cache parameter recommendations that can be applied via a safe rollout. The system should prioritize cost savings while enforcing latency SLOs and providing automated rollback on regression.

Scope: profiling agent (sampling pipeline), probabilistic workload model, heuristic rule engine, continuous parameter weaver (online tuning loop), safe-apply controller (canary, shadow-apply, rollback), observability and audit trail for each recommendation. Not in scope: model architecture changes, quantization engine work (separate project).

Success metrics (primary): 1) 5–15% net token-cost reduction for targeted routes within 6 weeks of rollout, 2) <5ms median added latency and p99 regressions <2% relative to baseline during canary, 3) zero customer-facing error incidents attributable to CostWeave rollout. Secondary: reduction in provisioning variance and fewer manual batching config edits by SREs.
acceptance_criteria: Profiling agent deployed to shadow tier for 10% of production traffic and collecting per-route sequence length distributions and KV cache hit estimates
Recommender emits candidate parameter sets (batch_size, microbatch_threshold, kv_cache_ttl, prefix_cache_enabled) with expected cost delta and risk score
Safe-apply controller supports 3-phase rollout: shadow -> canary (1% traffic) -> graduated rollout and automatic rollback trigger based on latency/cost regressions
Dashboard tile showing recommender suggestions, predicted savings, confidence, and audit log entries per recommendation
End-to-end integration test that simulates bursty traffic and verifies rollback when p99 increases > 2% over baseline
decisions: Use probabilistic mixture models (Gaussian + long-tail component) for per-route length profiling to better capture heavy-tailed prompts
Heuristic engine will prefer conservative parameter deltas for low-traffic customers (max 10% batch increase) and allow larger deltas for high-volume stable routes
Apply feature-flagged rollout with a controller outside the critical request path to avoid single-point failures in runtime
Store all recommendations and telemetry in time-indexed S3 buckets + Redshift for downstream analysis (links below)
implementation_notes: Agent: lightweight Rust sidecar that samples 1/100 requests for detailed traces and aggregates histograms every 60s
Recommender: batch offline job (Spark) to build initial priors; online tuner implemented as Go service using Thompson sampling over discretized parameter space
Safe-apply: Kubernetes operator that creates a canary deployment and traffic-slice with real-time alerting hooks to console-alerting and incident runbooks
Telemetry: add two new events: cost_recommendation.created and cost_recommendation.state_changed (for audit)
risks: Overfitting to sampled traces leads to aggressive batch increases that harm tail latency
Interplay between KV cache TTL and batching causing unexpected cache thrash for multi-turn chat routes
Incorrect rollback thresholds might oscillate and cause thrash between configurations
Edge customers with strict SLAs may object to automated config changes without explicit approval
mitigations: Conservative defaults + per-customer risk score that limits max parameter deltas
Require explicit opt-in for customers with SLA tag 'strict-sla' before any automated apply
Implement hysteresis in rollout controller to prevent flip-flop (min hold time + cooldown windows)
Run 72-hour shadow experiments for new heuristic families before enabling canaries
rollout_plan: Week 1: Deploy profiling agent to shadow tier for 10% of traffic; run nightly aggregation jobs
Week 2: Generate initial recommendations for low-risk routes; surface suggestions to Console under 'Suggested Optimizations' (no apply)
Week 3: Enable shadow-apply for 5% of traffic with telemetry collection; evaluate cost/latency deltas
Week 4: Canary apply to 1% traffic for routes with confidence > 0.7 and risk score < 0.3; automated rollback triggers enabled
Week 5–6: Gradual expansion and tune heuristics based on observed false-positive/false-negative signals
test_plan: Unit tests for sampling and histogram aggregation (target 90% coverage)
Integration test that runs the tuner against synthetic traces with known optima
E2E canary test that uses a load-generator to replicate burst patterns and validates rollback behavior
Chaos test: simulate agent failures and ensure controller does not apply partial configs
